target_customer: Merchants, enterprises, banks and global internet companies that need to accept and send payments in African markets
problem: Global payment providers such as Stripe and PayPal did not serve most African countries, so businesses struggled to accept cards, mobile money and bank payments across borders.
business_model: Payments take rate on transactions processed through APIs, plus fees on payouts, FX and added financial services
product_category: Payments infrastructure and fintech in Africa

founders.name: Iyinoluwa Aboyeji
founders.background_notes: The YC launch post (August 10 2016) names him as co-founder and says he previously ran Andela.

founders.name: Olugbenga Agboola
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; backgrounds not given there. The YC page says the team came from Standard Bank, Andela, PayPal and Google Wallet and others.

founders.name: Adeleke Adekoya
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; background not given there.

competitors.name: Stripe
competitors.what: Global payments API that, per the YC launch post, had not launched in African countries because payments were hard to process

competitors.name: PayPal
competitors.what: Global payments provider that excluded most African countries, per the YC launch post

competitors.name: Paystack
competitors.what: Nigerian payments startup in YC Winter 2016 focused on web payment collection for startups; its CEO said Flutterwave seemed aimed at sending and receiving money by any means via API (per a 2016 TechCabal piece seen in a search summary, page returned 403)

technical_complexity.rationale: A payments API layer over many local processors, mobile money and banks needed integrations, KYC, security and compliance across countries, which is demanding but standard payments engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Licences and local bank and processor integrations are slow to replicate and merchants integrate deeply, but competitors such as Paystack offered similar APIs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stripe acquired Paystack in 2020 per press, but I did not open a source for this; Flutterwave stayed independent, raised at over 3 billion dollars in 2022 and kept building African payment licences.

market_need_then: The YC launch post (August 2016) says Stripe and PayPal had avoided African markets because payments were difficult, and cites Uber facing limits on card payments in Lagos.

identity.logo: Butterfly logo before 2022; new identity by agency Verve launched in February 2022 with six primary colours and a brand library
identity.visual_style: Colourful identity celebrating African entrepreneurial spirit

branding.brand_signature: The 2022 colourful brand system and the butterfly mark

rebrands.why: Positioning beyond payments as a technology company, announced days after the 250 million raise (trade press).

branding.community_and_virality: Trade press and design press covered the rebrand, with some user criticism; no merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Widely known African fintech brand with design press coverage and large partner logos, though no source ties the name itself to growth.

pivots.from: Payments API for merchants and processors across Africa
pivots.to: Broader suite: consumer apps, banking, card issuing, lending and FaaS
pivots.why: Company site and rebrand coverage show expansion beyond payments; exact dates are not given.

outcome_analysis: Flutterwave launched in 2016 with a payments API for markets that Stripe and PayPal had skipped, raised a 10 million dollar Series A in 2017, 35 million in 2020, 170 million in March 2021 and 250 million in February 2022 at a valuation above 3 billion. Growth brought setbacks: reported layoffs in 2024 and 2025, and an alleged security breach in 2024, while licence applications in several countries remain in progress.
notes: Series A: sources conflict, with 10M in 2017 (Digest Africa) and an extension or second entry in 2018 (9.2M or 10M with Mastercard and Raba Capital per an aggregator); only the 2017 round is recorded and Digest Africa and Series B and C investor lists were seen in search summaries, not opened pages (techpoint and techcabal returned 403 or were not fetched). A 230K seed from Y Combinator in 2016 appears in one aggregator only, not recorded. Reports say Visa or FIS joined the Series B, unresolved. Total raised estimates run from 475M to 489M. An unverified single source reports a Series E in June 2026 led by Ripple; not recorded. Layoffs: about 3 percent of staff in June 2024 and 50 percent of Kenya and South Africa staff in July 2025 (TechCabal). Founder education and prior employers were not found in opened sources. The Stripe acquisition of Paystack claim was not verified with an opened page.
